questions.questionText: How does a Hash Map work internally under the hood? Explain how hash collisions occur and how techniques like Separate Chaining and Open Addressing resolve them, including worst-case time complexity.
expectedConcepts: Hash function & bucket indexing
Collision handling (Separate Chaining, Linear/Quadratic Probing)
Load factor & rehashing threshold (0.75)
Time complexity O(1) avg vs O(N) worst case
Java 8 Red-Black tree conversion for chains > 8
questions.sampleAnswerSummary: A hash map calculates bucket index using hash(key) & (n - 1). Collisions are resolved via linked lists / balanced trees or open addressing. When load factor exceeds 0.75, the table doubles in capacity and rehashes elements.
followUpStarters: What happens if all keys produce the exact same hash code?
Can you explain why resizing uses powers of two for bitwise AND masking?
How does thread safety impact Hash Map performance, and what is the difference with ConcurrentHashMap?

questions.questionText: Given an array of integers and a target sum, how would you design an optimal algorithm to find two numbers that sum to the target? Compare the time and space trade-offs between Brute Force, Hash Table, and Two Pointers on a sorted array.
expectedConcepts: Brute force O(N^2) time, O(1) space
Hash map single-pass O(N) time, O(N) space
Sorted array two-pointer O(N log N) or O(N) if pre-sorted, O(1) space
Edge cases: duplicates, negative numbers, overflow
questions.sampleAnswerSummary: For unsorted arrays with single pass, store complements (target - num) in a hash map for O(N) time and O(N) space. If space is constrained and array can be sorted in place, sorting + two pointers yields O(N log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
followUpStarters: How would you extend this approach to 3Sum or 4Sum without generating duplicate triplets?
What if the input stream is continuous and cannot fit into memory?
How does your algorithm handle duplicate pairs that sum to the target?

questions.questionText: How do you identify whether a problem has Optimal Substructure and Overlapping Subproblems? Walk me through how you would convert a recursive exponential solution into a dynamic programming solution using memoization and tabulation.
expectedConcepts: Identification of recursive state variables
Memoization top-down with recursion call stack
Tabulation bottom-up with iterative table filling
Space optimization by keeping only necessary previous states
Recurrence relation formulation
questions.sampleAnswerSummary: Optimal substructure means optimal solution of problem contains optimal solutions of subproblems. Overlapping subproblems means same subproblems are computed repeatedly. We define state dp[i], identify base cases, write transition equation, and optionally reduce space if only last k states are needed.
followUpStarters: Can you give an example where DP space complexity can be reduced from O(N) to O(1)?
What is the difference between 0/1 Knapsack and Unbounded Knapsack state transitions?
When is dynamic programming inferior to Greedy approaches?

questions.questionText: Explain the four ACID properties in relational database management systems with real-world banking transaction examples. What mechanisms does a database use to ensure Atomicity and Durability during system crashes?
expectedConcepts: Atomicity (all-or-nothing, rollback via Write-Ahead Logging/Undo log)
Consistency (schema constraints, foreign keys)
Isolation (concurrency control, Read Committed vs Serializable)
Durability (WAL, Redo log, checkpointing to disk)
Banking transfer example
questions.sampleAnswerSummary: ACID guarantees transactional integrity. Atomicity ensures debit and credit both succeed or roll back. Consistency maintains invariant constraints. Isolation prevents dirty reads and phantom reads. Durability writes logs to non-volatile storage before confirming commits via WAL.
followUpStarters: What are dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantom reads?
How does 2-Phase Locking (2PL) differ from Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC)?
Why would a high-throughput system choose eventual consistency over strong ACID guarantees?

questions.questionText: What is the difference between INNER JOIN, LEFT OUTER JOIN, and FULL JOIN? Furthermore, how does a B-Tree index work to accelerate SELECT queries, and what is the trade-off during INSERT/UPDATE operations?
expectedConcepts: Join types and Venn diagram/Cartesian matching
B-Tree index structure (root, branch, leaf nodes with pointers)
Lookup complexity reduction from O(N) full table scan to O(log N)
Index overhead on writes due to page splits and tree rebalancing
Composite index leftmost prefix rule
questions.sampleAnswerSummary: INNER JOIN returns matching records; LEFT JOIN returns all left rows plus matched right rows. B-Tree indexes maintain a sorted balanced hierarchy allowing O(log N) binary searches on disk blocks. Write operations slow down because every insert/update must rebalance index trees.
followUpStarters: What is the difference between a Clustered Index and a Non-Clustered Index?
Why should you not create an index on a boolean column with low cardinality?
How do you inspect query execution plans using EXPLAIN in PostgreSQL or MySQL?

questions.questionText: How does React's Virtual DOM and Reconciliation algorithm (Fiber) work? What happens under the hood when setState or useState is called, and why are unique keys essential when rendering lists?
expectedConcepts: Virtual DOM tree diffing (O(N) heuristic algorithm)
React Fiber incremental rendering and work loops
State batching in React 18
Keys for element identity tracking across re-renders to prevent unnecessary DOM mutations
Component lifecycle & useEffect dependencies
questions.sampleAnswerSummary: React maintains a lightweight in-memory representation of real DOM. When state changes, a new VDOM tree is constructed. React diffs the old and new trees using heuristic rules: different component types produce different trees, and unique keys allow matching elements across renders, minimizing direct real DOM manipulation.
followUpStarters: What is the difference between useMemo, useCallback, and React.memo?
Can you explain why React Fiber uses a singly-linked list tree structure instead of a standard recursion stack?
How does Concurrent Mode in React 18 enable interruptible rendering?

questions.questionText: Tell me about a situation during a project or academic team assignment where you had a strong technical disagreement with a peer or team lead. How did you handle it, what was the resolution, and what did you learn?
expectedConcepts: STAR framework (Situation, Task, Action, Result)
Focus on data and objective trade-offs over ego
Active listening and understanding counter-arguments

Disagree and Commit principle
questions.sampleAnswerSummary: Use STAR format: Describe project context (e.g. database choice or API architecture), articulate the specific difference of technical perspective, explain how you gathered data or benchmarked both solutions objectively, show the compromise reached, and conclude with the successful project metric outcome.
followUpStarters: If the team lead insisted on their approach despite benchmark evidence, how would you proceed?
What would you do differently if you were to encounter that exact scenario again today?

technicalProblems.title: SQL Second Highest & N-th Salary per Department
technicalProblems.description: Write an SQL query using window functions to find the second highest earning employee in each department without using subquery limit offsets.

starterCode.javascript:
-- Schema: Employee (id, name, salary, department_id), Department (id, name)
WITH RankedSalaries AS (
  SELECT 
    d.name AS department_name,
    e.name AS employee_name,
    e.salary,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.department_id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) AS salary_rank
  FROM Employee e
  JOIN Department d ON e.department_id = d.id
)
SELECT department_name, employee_name, salary
FROM RankedSalaries
WHERE salary_rank = 2;

testCases.expected: Outputs exact 2nd highest earner per department

defenseQuestions: What is the difference between RANK(), DENSE_RANK(), and ROW_NUMBER() during salary ties?
Explain how the database execution engine executes PARTITION BY vs GROUP BY.
How would you index the Employee table to optimize partition ordering?

technicalProblems.title: SQL Consecutive Logins & Active Day Streaks
technicalProblems.description: Find all users who logged in for at least 3 consecutive days. Table `Logins (user_id, login_date)`.

starterCode.javascript:
-- Table: Logins (user_id INT, login_date DATE)
WITH DistinctLogins AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_id, login_date FROM Logins
),
GroupedLogins AS (
  SELECT 
    user_id,
    login_date,
    DATEADD(day, -ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date), login_date) AS streak_group
  FROM DistinctLogins
)
SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS streak_days
FROM GroupedLogins
GROUP BY user_id, streak_group
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;

defenseQuestions: Explain the mathematical trick of subtracting ROW_NUMBER() from login_date to group streaks.
Why is `SELECT DISTINCT` mandatory before computing row numbers?
How would you optimize this query when Logins contains over 100 million rows?

questions.questionText: How does a Hash Map work internally under the hood? Explain collision handling with Separate Chaining vs Open Addressing.
questions.userAnswer: In a Hash Map, keys are converted into hash codes and mapped to bucket indices using bitwise masking. Collisions happen when two keys share the same bucket index. We resolve collisions through separate chaining using linked lists or red-black trees in Java 8, or open addressing using linear probing.

evaluation.strengths: Clearly explained bucket indexing, collision resolution methods, and Java 8 Red-Black tree conversion.

questions.questionText: Explain the four ACID properties in RDBMS with a banking transfer scenario.
questions.userAnswer: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability. In banking, when transferring 1000 rupees from Account A to B, both debit and credit must happen together or rollback (Atomicity). Constraints ensure total bank balance is preserved (Consistency). Concurrent transfers do not interfere with intermediate balances (Isolation). Changes are logged to disk via WAL before acknowledging (Durability).

evaluation.strengths: Exemplary real-world explanation using debit and credit transactions with WAL mention.
evaluation.improvements: Mention isolation levels like Repeatable Read and Serializable.

overallEvaluation.summary: High clarity on DBMS transactions and clean verbal delivery.
